title: Book a Driver Knowledge Test (DKT) in-person
summary: Book an in-person Driver Knowledge Test (DKT) at a Service NSW Centre to apply for a learner driver licence.
intro:
You can make a booking to take the Driver Knowledge Test (DKT) in-person at a Service NSW Centre.

Once you pass the DKT you can apply for your learner driver licence.

The DKT in-person is available in Greek, Turkish, Croatian, Serbian, English, Arabic, Simplified Chinese, Korean, Spanish and Vietnamese. Interpreter and other support is also available.

If you live with a disability, make an appointment with your medical specialist before you go to the service centre. They will be able to advise you if any additional information will be required, such as a medical assessment.

If these conditions don't apply to you, you can take the DKT online.
who_can_apply: Must take the DKT in-person if the conditions for online testing do not apply
what_you_need: Your name and date of birth, or your NSW Photo Card number (if you have one)
Payment (unless you are eligible for a fee waiver)
Your contact lenses or glasses (if you wear them)
Proof of identity documentation (Note: Commemorative certificates are not accepted)
To book the DKT, you will need to follow the online booking steps.

how_to_steps.text: Follow the prompts to book a DKT.

more_info.text: To study for the test you can use the NSW practice test online or download the practice test app from the App Store or Google Play.
You should also read the Road User Handbook and view the test questions.
If you do not pass the DKT, you can sit the test again on the same day if another booking is available.
You can take your test in a quieter environment at a Quiet Hour service centre location.

Additional needs – if you have trouble reading test questions our staff can assist by reading the questions and explaining them to you.

faqs.q: What happens after I pass the DKT?
faqs.a: Once you pass the DKT, you can apply for your learner driver licence.

faqs.q: Are there language options for the DKT?
faqs.a: The DKT in-person is available in Greek, Turkish, Croatian, Serbian, English, Arabic, Simplified Chinese, Korean, Spanish, and Vietnamese. Interpreter and other support is also available.

faqs.q: Do I need to make an appointment if I have a disability?
faqs.a: If you live with a disability, make an appointment with your medical specialist before you go to the service centre. They will advise if any additional information, such as a medical assessment, is required.
